_notes: X-Men Limited Edition (V1.51 Home) - Stern SAM platform.
NOT independently published anywhere we could find (not in tomlogic/pinmame-nvram-maps as of 2026-08-17).
Derived by pattern-matching ScoresData/nvram/xmn_151h.nv against the documented layout for other
same-era Stern SAM2 titles (avs_170, smanve_101, twd_156) from https://github.com/tomlogic/pinmame-nvram-maps.
Those titles use: 11-byte null-terminated ASCII initials + 4-byte little-endian int score per slot,
0x20-byte stride between slots, unused bytes filled with 0xFF, NO checksum over the high-score region.
xmn_151h.nv matches that same shape at file offset 0x3000 (CPU address 0x02103000).
CONFIDENCE: medium. Internally consistent and matches the platform convention, but the sample .nv file
in ScoresData appears to be synthetic demo data (its Grand Champion score/tail bytes are byte-for-byte
identical to avs_170.nv's, which real independent play would not produce) - so this has NOT been
confirmed against a genuine captured dump of this exact ROM. Needs real-machine verification.
File offset = CPU address - 0x02100000 (NVRAM is mapped at 0x02100000 per platforms/stern-sam.json).
A 6th slot at file offset 0x30A0 ('YAN', counter=15) looks like a mode-champion counter (small int,
not a full score) analogous to smanve_101's mode_champions entries - not verified, not used for testing.
CHECKSUM (2026-08-17): disassembled smanve_101.bin (Spider-Man Vault Edition ROM, different game,
same Stern SAM platform) and found the real checksum: tag (2 bytes @ record+0x1c) = 0xFFFF - (sum of
the 28 bytes from record start through the score field, mod 65536). Confirmed 24/24 against real
smanve_101 data. This algorithm is presumed (NOT independently confirmed) to apply identically here -
it's a generic runtime-library checksum, not game-specific logic, and the xmn_151h.nv sample's own G S,
L R, etc. entries and their tag bytes are consistent with this formula (spot-checked, matches), but we
don't have a real captured X-Men NVRAM with genuine player data to fully cross-verify the way we did
for Spider-Man. research/patch_nvram_score.py now computes this automatically for both tables.
